metaDescription: Six Ryobi cordless leaf blowers compared across the 18V ONE+ and 40V platforms, from a 250 CFM sweeper to the 800 CFM Whisper Series, by yard size.
expertTake: The 40V HP Whisper 650 CFM model is the best fit for most large lots, while the 40V 550 CFM is the value pick if you own other 40V tools. Owners of the 18V ONE+ system should take the 350 CFM jet fan blower for general work and the compact brushless unit for tight spaces. If you own neither battery family and have a large property, look at a different brand's backpack.
introParagraphs: Home-center cordless brands build everything around a battery that fits dozens of tools, and the blower is often the cheapest way to put an existing pack to work. That makes the sums different from a stand-alone tool: the same machine can be a bargain or an overpriced extra depending on what is already in your garage.

The lineup is split across two battery systems of different size, and the blowers on each reach very different power levels. Reading the label correctly is the main skill in this category, since a small-platform tool and a large-platform tool can wear the same logo and look similar on a shelf.

products.name: Ryobi 40V HP Brushless Whisper Blower 800 CFM 180 MPH
products.description:
The top of the Ryobi blower range pairs 800 CFM with 180 MPH from a 40V HP brushless motor. Those two numbers together are what you want for heavy piles and wet leaves, because the volume shifts the load and the speed lifts it from the ground. It sits in the Whisper Series, which is Ryobi's lower-noise line.

The listing is for the bare tool, so battery and charger are extra. Compared with the 650 CFM sibling at 160 MPH, it adds 150 CFM and 20 MPH, which is a clear step up in capability rather than a marginal one. Against the 40V 550 CFM model at 120 MPH, the gap is larger still. The HP designation points to a higher-performance motor and electronics designed to deliver that power from a 40V pack.

Because the tool does not include a battery, plan on a big 40V pack, ideally 6.0Ah or larger, as a small one will empty quickly at this output. Brush the intake after each session, avoid leaving packs in a hot vehicle and store them partly charged. It is the right pick for acreage, wet leaf seasons and anyone who wants a handheld to compete with gas.
products.bestFor: Large lots and wet leaf seasons for owners with 40V packs.
pros: 800 CFM and 180 MPH from a brushless motor
Whisper Series for lower noise
Shares the 40V Ryobi battery family
Strongest Ryobi handheld in the guide
cons: Bare tool without battery or charger
Needs a large pack to run at full output

products.name: Ryobi 40V HP Brushless Whisper Blower 650 CFM 160 MPH
products.description:
The 650 CFM Whisper is the step below the 800 CFM flagship, and for most homeowners it is the smarter buy. It lists 650 CFM and 160 MPH from a 40V HP brushless motor in the same low-noise Whisper family. For half an acre or so of dry and damp leaves, it has all the force you need.

Compared with the 40V 550 CFM model at 120 MPH, it moves about 18 percent more air and a third more speed, which shows up as faster work on thick leaf cover. Compared with the 800 CFM unit, you give up 150 CFM, but you save weight and money. It is a bare tool, so budget for a pack.

Treat the quoted figures as peak numbers at the top setting. Run the middle of the dial for most of a job and save turbo for stuck patches, which preserves battery life. Clear the intake after use and check the nozzle for cracks every season.
products.bestFor: Half-acre lots with a mix of dry and damp leaves.
pros: 650 CFM and 160 MPH
Whisper Series for lower noise
Brushless HP motor with long life
Cheaper and lighter than the 800 CFM model
cons: Tool only, so a pack is extra

products.name: Ryobi 40V Blower RY40LB01B 550 CFM 120 MPH

specList.label: Listing
specList.value: Tool only; no battery or charger

products.description:
The RY40LB01B is the plain 40V blower: 550 CFM, 120 MPH and no frills. It is described as suitable for leaves and debris, and the listing is firm that the battery and charger are not included. A renewed kit version of the same blower with a 4.0Ah battery and charger also appears on the market, which is useful for anyone starting from nothing.

Its virtue is price and simplicity. It gives you more than two times the airflow of the 18V models without the HP price premium. Against the 650 CFM Whisper, it is lower in both volume and speed, and it does not belong to the quieter series.

If you already own 40V Ryobi packs and a mower or trimmer, this is the cheapest route to a real yard blower. Clean the intake each time, keep a spare pack if you can and store the tool indoors over winter.
products.bestFor: Existing 40V owners who want a capable blower at low cost.
pros: 550 CFM and 120 MPH on the 40V platform
Lower cost than the HP Whisper models
Simple, easy-to-use controls
Works with the whole 40V battery family
cons: Not in the low-noise Whisper line

products.name: Ryobi ONE+ 18V PCLLB01B Jet Fan Blower 350 CFM 100 MPH
products.description:
The PCLLB01B is the 18V ONE+ jet fan blower with a variable-speed trigger, quoting 350 CFM and 100 MPH. It is positioned for light work, hard surfaces and dry leaves, and it requires no fuel or cord. The ONE+ system is Ryobi's mainstream battery line, shared by dozens of tools, so existing owners can use it right away.

Compared with the 250 CFM P21011, it moves about 40 percent more air at 10 MPH higher speed, which is a worthwhile step for a small price difference. Compared with the 40V models, it is a size smaller: 350 against 550 CFM. For a small suburban lot that is enough.

Battery and charger are sold separately, and a 4.0Ah pack suits it better than a small one. Keep the jet fan intake clean and avoid using it to blow wet debris, which will clog the guard. It is a sensible first blower for an 18V household, and it pairs well with the trimmer and drill that probably came with your first battery.
products.bestFor: Small to medium lots for owners already on the 18V ONE+ system.
pros: 350 CFM and 100 MPH on the 18V platform
Variable-speed trigger
Shares the huge ONE+ battery family
No fuel or cord
cons: Too light for heavy or wet leaves

products.name: Ryobi ONE+ 18V P21011 Blower 250 CFM 90 MPH
products.description:
The P21011 is Ryobi's compact, lightweight 18V blower, quoting 250 CFM and 90 MPH. The listing positions it for hard surfaces such as sidewalks and driveways, and the main selling point is that it needs no maintenance like a gas blower does. It is the least powerful tool in this guide.

That makes it a tool for sweeping rather than clearing. It pushes grass clippings and dry leaves off pavement but will not shift a thick layer on a lawn. If you want more airflow on the same battery family, the 350 CFM jet fan model is the next step.

Because it is a bare tool, it only makes sense if you own ONE+ batteries. A small pack is adequate for its low draw. Wipe the nozzle after use, store the tool without the battery attached and treat it as a garage broom.
products.bestFor: Sweeping sidewalks and driveways for existing 18V owners.
pros: Compact and lightweight for easy use
No gas, no maintenance
Cheapest entry to a Ryobi blower
Runs on any ONE+ battery

products.name: Ryobi ONE+ 18V HP Brushless Compact Blower RY18BLCXA
products.description:
The RY18BLCXA is billed as Ryobi's lightest and most compact leaf blower, and it uses the HP brushless motor on the 18V platform. A variable-speed trigger controls the power, and the length can be customised, with two different nozzles included. The listing gives no CFM or MPH figures, so I will not quote any.

Its job is tight spaces: decks, window wells, car interiors and garage corners. The brushless motor makes it more efficient than the plain P21011, so you get more runtime from the same battery. Against the 350 CFM jet fan model, it is smaller and quieter, but is not meant for a lawn.

Use the shorter nozzle setup for tight work and the longer one for reach. Wipe it down after dusty jobs and store it with the battery removed. It is the best choice in this guide for a tool that spends more time in a truck bed than on a lawn.
products.bestFor: Tight spaces, decks and vehicle cleaning on the 18V ONE+ platform.
pros: Lightest and most compact Ryobi blower
Brushless HP motor for efficiency
Two nozzles with customisable length
Variable-speed trigger
cons: No airflow figures on the listing

buyingCriteria.criterion: Pick the platform before the blower
buyingCriteria.explanation: Ryobi sells blowers on 18V ONE+ and 40V platforms, and the packs do not cross. The 18V models top out at 350 CFM here, while the 40V models run from 550 to 800 CFM. If you own ONE+ batteries, the 18V tools are cheap, but if you have a large lot, the 40V line is the only one with real power. Do not buy a platform just for one blower, since the batteries are the long-term cost.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Understand the HP and Whisper names
buyingCriteria.explanation: HP stands for the high-performance brushless line, and Whisper marks the lower-noise series. Both the 650 CFM and 800 CFM models are HP Whisper tools. A standard 40V blower such as the RY40LB01B at 550 CFM is quieter than gas but not in the Whisper line. If neighbours or noise rules matter, the Whisper designation is worth the premium.

The 800 CFM Whisper lists 180 MPH, the 650 CFM model 160 MPH and the plain 40V 120 MPH. A bigger CFM moves more leaves while a higher MPH lifts stuck ones, so both numbers should rise together in a better tool. The 18V models at 250 and 350 CFM sit well below, and suit light work only.

A blower is one of the hungriest tools on a battery. A 2.0Ah pack may last only a few minutes at full output, while a 6.0Ah or larger pack gives far longer. The HP Whisper models in particular benefit from large packs. If your listing is tool-only, add the cost of a decent pack to your sums.

The 800 CFM, 650 CFM, 550 CFM, 350 CFM and 250 CFM listings here are tool-only. A renewed 550 CFM kit with a 4.0Ah battery and charger also exists. A bare tool is a saving only if you already own packs, and a kit is better for newcomers.

The compact RY18BLCXA includes two nozzles and a customisable length, which makes it flexible for tight work. The larger 40V models are better for open ground. A good blower should feel balanced in your hand, so if you have wrist trouble, favour the lighter 18V tools for short sessions.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow ladder
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each blower on a ladder from 250 CFM up to 800 CFM and compared speed at each step. The ladder shows that the 18V line is for light work and the 40V line for real yards.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform logic
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered the two battery systems and how sharing packs affects value. An 18V blower is cheap for an 18V household, and a 40V blower is cheap for a 40V one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted which models belong to the Whisper Series and which are compact. Comfort over a 20 minute job counted for as much as the peak figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Kit completeness
howWeEvaluated.description: We flagged tool-only listings and the added cost of a pack. A model that includes a battery changes the real cost, and we said so where it applies.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership outlook
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, brushless HP motors and simple designs score well for long life. We did not guess at missing figures.

cards.label: 18V ONE+
cards.text: The P21011, PCLLB01B and RY18BLCXA. Light and cheap, with batteries shared across many tools. Best for small lots and quick cleanups.

cards.label: 40V
cards.text: The 550, 650 and 800 CFM models. Much more airflow and the only Ryobi tools with real power for large yards.

howToChoose.note: Take 18V for lots under a quarter acre; take 40V for anything bigger.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High air speed and a large battery. Wet leaves bond to the ground, so a narrow fast stream is far better than a wide gentle one.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 800 CFM Whisper at 180 MPH and the 650 CFM model at 160 MPH are the ones to buy. The 18V models are best left to dry leaves.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clear for 30 minutes or more or deal with wet leaves each autumn. The HP Whisper models are worth it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You sweep a small area occasionally. The P21011 or PCLLB01B with a battery you own is plenty.

maintenance.why: Leaf scraps block the intake and heat the motor. A quick brush restores airflow.
A cracked nozzle on the RY18BLCXA or Whisper models disrupts the air stream and loses speed. Replace it if it splits.
Lithium packs age fastest stored full, empty or cold. Keep them indoors and dry.
A blower empties a pack quickly. Swapping to a second battery avoids deep discharge and heat.
Dust in the vents holds heat, and grit in the trigger makes it sticky. A dry cloth keeps both clean.

faq.q: Which Ryobi blower is best for most people?
faq.a: For large lots, the 40V HP Whisper 650 CFM model offers the best balance of power and cost. For a small yard on the 18V system, the PCLLB01B at 350 CFM is the sensible pick.

faq.q: Is the 800 CFM Whisper worth the extra over the 650 CFM?
faq.a: It adds 150 CFM and 20 MPH, which helps with heavy and wet leaves. For half-acre lots of mostly dry leaves, the 650 CFM model is enough.
The listings here are tool-only. A renewed 550 CFM kit with a 4.0Ah battery and charger exists, but check the condition and model number carefully.

faq.q: Can I use 18V batteries in the 40V blowers?
faq.a: No. The 18V ONE+ and 40V families are separate and do not interchange. Buy the pack that matches the blower.

faq.q: What does the Whisper Series mean?
faq.a: It is Ryobi's lower-noise blower line. The listings do not give a decibel figure, so treat it as a design intent and compare by ear if you can.

faq.q: Is the compact brushless blower strong enough for leaves?
faq.a: Not for a lawn. The RY18BLCXA is for tight spaces, decks and vehicles. For leaf clearing, choose the 350 CFM or one of the 40V models.
